statement: Does the 35-vertex counterexample graph $H$ of openai/math family 161 satisfy the Kohayakawa-Nagle-Rodl-Schacht inequality, that is, does every $(\rho,d)$-dense graph sequence contain at least $(1-o(1))d^{66}n^{35}$ homomorphic copies of $H$ for suitable $\rho = \rho(d)$?

source.reference: Conlon, Kim, Lee and Lee (2018) state the KNRS conjecture and its link to subdivisions; the counterexample's host kernel is not shown to be locally dense.

observation: The KNRS conjecture restricts hosts to locally dense graphs and is implied by Sidorenko for bipartite patterns; the counterexample does not decide whether locally dense hosts can carry its deficit.
neighbours: Is the KNRS conjecture true for every bipartite graph?
Can the counterexample's kernel be modified to be locally dense?
notes: The KNRS literature (Bradac-Sudakov-Wigderson 2024, Chen-Lin-Ma 2024, Reiher 2014) is not read in full.

disposition.reason: Readiness: the decisive KNRS literature is not read in full.
disposition.evidence_needed: Full readings of the KNRS literature and an analysis of whether the counterexample's kernel is locally dense.
